headline: Khaitan & Co acts on HFCL ₹555 crore preferential issue
sum: HFCL Limited announces a preferential issue of 7.5 crore warrants aggregating ₹555 crore to the Promoter and Promoter Group. The transaction is being advised by Khaitan & Co.
implication: Preferential warrant issuances to promoters require shareholder approval and SEBI DIP compliance; this structuring preserves equity cushion while deploying capital to core stakeholders—a common recapitalisation tool in telecom.
detail: HFCL, a technology company specialising in telecommunications equipment, fiber-optic cables and defence-sector solutions, is conducting a preferential issue of 7.5 crore warrants valued at ₹555 crore to its Promoter and Promoter Group. Khaitan & Co's transaction team, led by Executive Director Sudhir Bassi and Partner Vaibhav Mittal, is managing the structuring and regulatory approvals. This issuance follows HFCL's recent ₹550 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP).

framework.note: Preferential allotment of securities requires shareholder approval by special resolution and compliance with Rule 13 (Preferential Allotment Rules)

framework.ref: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Reg. 81–83
framework.note: Pricing formula, lock-in, and disclosure norms for preferential allotments; warrants treated as convertible securities

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, s. 23
framework.note: Regulator's power to issue directions for preferential issuances to related parties or promoters

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Reg. 34(1)(d), 42
framework.note: Public company disclosure obligations, prior board/shareholder approval, material event notification to exchanges
Preferential issue disclosure, EGM intimation, trading halt (if applicable) during approval window
Consideration for preferential allotment determines tax treatment of premium, if any

framework.ref: SEBI Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulations, 2015
framework.note: Trading windows restricted for promoters and insiders during preferential issue window and until public disclosure

structure.consideration: ₹555 crore (7.5 crore warrants at proportionate pricing to Promoter and Promoter Group)
conditions: Shareholder approval by special resolution at General Meeting
SEBI pricing formula compliance (Rule 13, ICDR Regs 2018)
Board approval of preferential issue terms
Exercise of warrants conversion rights within stipulated period (typically 18 months from allotment)
structure.novel: Preferential warrant structure (rather than direct equity) allows promoters to defer equity dilution while securing subscription rights, useful in capital-constrained telecom sector.
